findings.claim_defeated: 'What is implemented is the subset of its syntax this repository uses: a directory pattern ending in `/`, a glob, a plain name, and a `!` negation. An anchored or path-bearing pattern is matched against the member-relative path as well as the name. That is narrower than git's own matching and is stated as such.'
findings.observed: The direction is wrong for the syntax actually in that file. _ignore_patterns strips `/` from both ends of every pattern, so a directory pattern is not implemented as a directory pattern at all - it becomes a plain name, and _matches tests it against every path component. Twenty-four of the forty-three patterns in .gitignore are directory patterns. The consequence is over-exclusion, not under-exclusion: a plain FILE named build, dist, env, venv, blobs or payloads is excluded here and kept by git. I built a throwaway repository holding this exact .gitignore and compared `git check-ignore -q` with _is_artifact over fifteen controlled paths: nine diverge, and all nine are the matcher excluding something git keeps. Anchoring is dropped by the same strip, so a future `/build` would exclude every `build` at any depth. _matches' own docstring says it matches 'one of its parents', and its candidate list holds path components rather than parent paths, so a multi-segment pattern like `docs/build/` would not exclude `docs/build/x` - there is no such pattern in the file today. None of this reaches the repository as it stands: my sweep over all 1477 tracked paths against every possible directory base found zero swallowed. The claim the delta actually makes - nothing tracked is swallowed - reproduces. This finding is about the sentence, and about the direction a future tracked file would fall.
findings.why_it_matters: The whole point of the repair is that a file the repository keeps must reach the digest. The one direction the docstring does not warn about is the one where a file the repository keeps stops reaching the digest, silently, because a name collided with a directory pattern. 'Narrower than git' tells a reader the opposite of what to watch for. It is also the exact shape 6a names: the deviation from the declaration it reads is real, currently harmless, and undescribed.

q1_landing_at_built.question: Do you object to landing at BUILT?

The container half is contradicted by pass4.json's own independence block, unrecorded for passes 1 through 3, and disowned by the same note 120 words later. The code repairs hold in every direction I could attack them: no tracked path is swallowed, all six planted ignored forms are excluded, the identity is one value across three trees including one that ran verify.py, the collision is closed, all three loosenings go red, declaration.py is byte-identical so no oracle was weakened, verify and lint pass in a fresh clone on two readings, origin/main is an ancestor and gains two checks and loses none, no secret shape, no absolute path, no CRLF, no module over the ceiling, no file outside the concern, no vocabulary drift, and no standing claimed anywhere. The member reads standing BUILT, work_state PRESENTED, stage_observed_by null, and its own closing sentence still says 'BUILT only. A test may not claim WITNESSED.' Nothing in the delta claims otherwise.
q1_landing_at_built.note_on_the_objection: This is an objection to landing these bytes, not a reopening of the BUILT -> WITNESSED refusal, which stands and is not mine to revisit. If the concern holder judges that the two sentences are loose rather than false, that is a reading available to them and I have given the evidence rather than only the verdict. I applied the test I was given: a false statement in a governed record blocks. Both are one-clause repairs inside the concern and neither needs another ticket.

objection_to_landing_at_built: OBJECTION. Two false sentences in contracts/custodies/phase-1-5.json: the assertion that every reading came from one container, and the count of six withdrawals where the block holds seven. Both are in the file that carries the member's standing. Both are repairable in place without touching code, tests, fixtures or the standing itself.

verdict: REPRODUCED on every command and every code repair, WITH DISSENT on two sentences in a governed contract file, which is an objection to landing these exact bytes. All five delta claims reproduce; two of them I confirmed causally against pre-repair controls rather than reading them off the prose. The code half of this delta is the strongest on the branch after 964abd7: the identity now survives a fresh clone, a shared checkout that has imported the service many times, and a full verify run, at one value; the collision is closed; three loosenings that passed everything at 964abd7 now go red by name; and declaration.py was not touched, so nothing was relaxed to make it so. The delta rewrote a paragraph specifically to stop asserting unchecked facts about the readings, and the paragraph it wrote asserts that all ten readings ran in one container, which pass 4's own record contradicts and the same note disowns 120 words later. That is the fourth container claim in this file and the fourth time it has not been derived from the artifact. Ten findings, two blocking, both single-clause and both repairable inside the concern.
standing_supported: NONE. This observation supports no standing transition. The member stays BUILT at work_state PRESENTED, and the refusal of BUILT -> WITNESSED recorded by passes 1 through 10 is not reopened and is not affected by anything here. This record is an observation and grants nothing; it is not a settlement and not a acceptance. It does not support OPEN -> BUILT either, which is already held.

That is a question about the loop, not about this member, and no reading inside the loop can answer it.
